Flagged here rather than silently absorbed.

mechanism.summary: heartbeat_core.py picks bold's strike from the OTM-2 tier before it has priced the option at all, then kills the plan at the floor once the real (thin) premium comes back -- credentials and the order path are not the problem.
mechanism.strike_pick: setup/scripts/heartbeat_core.py:2616 -- `strike = ss.pick_strike(spy, equity, side, ss.V15_BOLD_TIERS if account == "bold" else ss.V15_SAFE_TIERS) ...`. For bold's $2,000-$10,000 equity band, `crypto/lib/strike_selection.py`'s `V15_BOLD_TIERS` (line 55) resolves `StrikeTier(2_000.0, 10_000.0, -2, "OTM-2")` -- spot ~765 => strike 767.
mechanism.premium_floor: setup/scripts/heartbeat_core.py:2664-2668 -- `_min_prem = _params_float(params, "min_entry_premium", 0.0); if _min_prem > 0 and mid < _min_prem: return {"status": "SKIP_MIN_PREMIUM_FLOOR", ...}`. This runs at PLAN time, strictly BEFORE `qty` sizing and BEFORE `rg.check_order` (risk_gate) is ever called -- an afternoon 0.07-0.11 OTM-2 premium never reaches risk_gate, it dies here.
mechanism.the_collision_was_pre_measured: crypto/lib/strike_selection.py's own V15_BOLD_CORE_TIERS docstring (lines 83-90) records this exact collision BEFORE today: 'OTM-3 at this tier shows a structural floor-collision (afternoon premium-floor clearance 0.3376, i.e. ~66% of afternoon signals never clear min_entry_premium and are silently skipped) and -$14.37/tr OOS; ATM clears floor at 0.9688 afternoon / 0.9795 overall and is +$28.77/tr OOS'. The $2K-$10K band was the OTM-3 table's neighbor (OTM-2, same failure mode) before the 2026-08-04 ATM-TIER-EXTENSION-2K-10K change folded it into the ATM-clearing table -- and that fold was itself reverted on 2026-08-20 (see below).
mechanism.order_path_is_fine: Bold placed and closed real round-trip fills as recently as 2026-08-21 (automation/state/logs/eod-flatten-aggressive-2026-08-21.log: 'AGG_RECONCILE_FLAG: 4 today-fills on aggressive... SPY260821C00768000 x2 round-trips, SPY260821P00763000 x1 round-trip') -- 3 round-trip real fills 4 sessions ago. Credentials, MCP wiring, and the order-placement path are demonstrably live; today's zero-trade day is a PLAN-time floor kill, not a broken pipe.

candidate_rule.provenance: Adapted from automation/state/fleet/fleet_executor.py's floor_rescue_plan (~lines 1136-1169), wired at automation/state/fleet/fleet_live.py (~lines 417-443), guarded by automation/state/fleet/test_floor_rescue_2026_08_03.py -- NOT the same file path the task brief cited (backtest/tests/), corrected here after reading the actual tree. NOT a blind port: fleet's version rescues a FULL_SEND lane plan_all already generates at PROBE_STRIKE_TIERS (a standalone ATM-class table, distinct from V15_BOLD_CORE_TIERS); core bold's heartbeat_core.py has no FULL_SEND/PROBE_ARM/SCORE_LADDER lane structure at all -- it is one linear per-tick path -- so this candidate is a new design in bold's structure, using fleet's ORDERING FIX as precedent, not its code.
candidate_rule.rule: On a tick where heartbeat_core.py's ENTER_BULL/ENTER_BEAR verdict for account==bold dies with status SKIP_MIN_PREMIUM_FLOOR at the V15_BOLD_TIERS-priced strike: re-price ONCE at the strike V15_BOLD_CORE_TIERS would select for the same equity band (today: ATM, offset 0, for the $2K-$10K band), fetch that strike's real premium (one additional get_option_mid + marketable_limit_price call, no order placed), re-run the SAME min_entry_premium floor check against the new premium, and -- ONLY if it clears -- re-run the full rg.check_order risk_gate against the new symbol/premium/qty. Any risk_gate deny on the rescue (RISK_CAP, PDT, NOT_FLAT, KILL_SWITCH, or the floor again) resolves the tick as the ORIGINAL SKIP_MIN_PREMIUM_FLOOR verdict, annotated with the rescue's own deny code for the audit trail -- never a silent second attempt.
eligibility_all_required_fail_closed: account == "bold" only. Safe's $2K-$10K band is already ATM under V15_SAFE_TIERS (crypto/lib/strike_selection.py lines 62-63) -- it does not have this collision and this candidate never touches safe.

decision.risk_code == "SKIP_MIN_PREMIUM_FLOOR" on the BASE V15_BOLD_TIERS-priced strike. Any other deny code is a real risk refusal that binds on the rescue identically; re-planning would be noise (mirrors fleet's own eligibility check).

NO per-setup strike override fired this tick. heartbeat_core.py's _SETUP_STRIKE_OVERRIDES branch (the block immediately after line 2616, before `expiry = _et_now()`) already re-prices certain validated setups (e.g. vwap_continuation) to their OWN tier-specific offset. If that branch already produced the strike, this tick already tried a near-money price and the floor kill on IT is a real, already-considered failure -- rescuing it a second time at a DIFFERENT (V15_BOLD_CORE_TIERS) offset would silently stack an unvalidated override on top of a validated one. This candidate's `NORMAL-lane ENTER` condition, restated precisely for heartbeat_core.py's actual structure (which has no FULL_SEND/PROBE_ARM/SCORE_LADDER lanes): the killed plan's strike came from the base V15_BOLD_TIERS pick_strike call, not from a _SETUP_STRIKE_OVERRIDES branch.
fires exactly once per tick -- no loop. The rescue strike is never itself re-rescued if it also floor-blocks.
candidate_rule.explicitly_out_of_scope: setup/scripts/j_intent_executor.py (the J-called conditional-trade path) is DELIBERATELY NOT given this rescue in this candidate. A J-called trade is a manually parameterized decision; silently substituting a different strike underneath it when the floor kills J's chosen strike is a different judgment call than rescuing the autonomous engine's own pick, and this prereg does not bundle the two. If this candidate is ever implemented, it must ship EITHER as heartbeat_core.py-only with a NEW guard test asserting j_intent_executor.py's floor-block path is UNCHANGED (still returns the plain floor SKIP, no rescue) -- making the asymmetry a tested, deliberate choice -- OR as both paths together, decided explicitly in that implementation session, never by silent drift. See two_site_invariant below for why this matters.

what_is_being_traded_off: V15_BOLD_CORE_TIERS is not a neutral 'nearer strike' -- it is THE table the 2026-08-20 rail measured negative and reverted. Wiring any rescue that reads from it is partially re-litigating that revert. BUT the rail's -$808/n=25 population is NOT the same population this candidate touches: the 2026-07-18 wire replaced V15_BOLD_TIERS OUTRIGHT at the heartbeat_core.py call site, so its n=25 fills are a MIX of (a) ticks that would have cleared the floor fine at OTM-2 pricing but were forcibly re-priced ATM anyway, and (b) ticks that would have floor-blocked at OTM-2 and were only tradeable because of the ATM reprice. This candidate's rescue ONLY ever fires on population (b) -- by construction it never touches a tick that already clears the floor at OTM-2, because the rescue only activates AFTER a SKIP_MIN_PREMIUM_FLOOR verdict. The rail's aggregate verdict cannot be read as a verdict on population (b) alone; it conflates the two. Separating 'rescue helps' from 'ATM helps' requires measuring population (b) on its own, against its own true counterfactual -- $0 P&L (no trade), NOT the OTM-2 baseline (which never traded these ticks at all) and NOT the rail's mixed-population aggregate (which is the wrong denominator for this question).

measurement_protocol.mode: SHADOW ONLY. No rescue ever places a live order or replaces a live SKIP_MIN_PREMIUM_FLOOR verdict during this window. On every qualifying floor-block (bold, base-tier SKIP_MIN_PREMIUM_FLOOR, no setup override fired), compute the V15_BOLD_CORE_TIERS strike, fetch its real premium via the SAME read-only calls the live tick already makes (get_option_mid, marketable_limit_price) -- zero new network round-trip pattern, one extra symbol -- and log a shadow row. No order is placed.
measurement_protocol.where: planned: analysis/recommendations/bold-floor-rescue-shadow-ledger.jsonl (house convention -- see day-throttle-shadow-ledger.jsonl / catastrophe-cap-shadow-ledger.jsonl / stop-mode-shadow-ledger.jsonl for the existing pattern). Not created by this file -- a future implementation session creates it when shadow logging is actually wired.
measurement_protocol.window: next 15 trading sessions with at least one bold SKIP_MIN_PREMIUM_FLOOR event (not 15 calendar sessions -- floor-blocks are not daily; today (2026-08-25) alone produced several, so 15 EVENTS is expected to arrive faster than 15 sessions).
measurement_protocol.no_peeking_rule: no interim wiring of the rescue into the live order path, no threshold edits, no re-picking the rescue table mid-window. If the table or eligibility rule needs to change, this pre-registration is void and a new one is written.
measurement_protocol.cost: $0 -- one extra read-only option-quote fetch per floor-block event (a handful of times per session at most, per today's entry-block-watch cadence).

forward_gates.F1_frequency: n_shadow_events >= 15 rescue-eligible floor-blocks (otherwise EXTEND, judge nothing)
forward_gates.F2_participation_unlock: rescue_would_clear_floor rate >= 0.70 across the shadow population -- if the ATM-class rescue ALSO fails the floor most of the time, this is not a participation fix, it is noise (compare against the V15_BOLD_CORE_TIERS docstring's own 0.9688/0.3376 pattern, acknowledging the $2K-$10K band is a different cell than the one that produced those exact numbers)
forward_gates.F3_simulated_pnl_vs_zero: sum of simulated forward P&L on the rescue-cleared cohort (mark-to-real-exit using the SAME exit rules the live engine would have applied, computed offline from OPRA/quote history, never live) > $0 -- the correct baseline is $0 (no trade), not the OTM-2 population's WR/P&L
forward_gates.F4_not_a_loser_unlock: rescue-cleared cohort's simulated WR >= 0.24 (the ATM tier's OWN measured worst-case WR from the 2026-08-20 rail, n=25) -- if the rescue cohort performs WORSE than the exact tier the rail already killed, this candidate inherits that verdict rather than escaping it
forward_gates.F5_risk_gate_integrity: 100% of shadow rows show a full rg.check_order re-run at the rescue's real premium/qty (not skipped, not stubbed) -- a shadow logging integrity gate, not a P&L gate; a shadow row that skips this is void and does not count toward F1-F4
forward_gates.F6_no_setup_override_leakage: 0% of shadow rows fire when a _SETUP_STRIKE_OVERRIDES branch already produced the killed plan's strike -- if this ever happens the eligibility check has a bug and the window is void from that point

verdict_ladder.ARM: F1-F6 all pass -- proceed to a real (still shadow, still no live orders) implementation PR with its own guard tests, THEN a live A/B
verdict_ladder.EXTEND: F1 fails (too few events) -- run 15 more sessions or until 15 events accumulate, judge nothing
verdict_ladder.KILL: F2, F3, or F4 fails, or F5/F6 fail (instrumentation is broken, re-build before re-measuring)

kill_criterion_precommitted: If, after the shadow window closes, the rescue-cleared cohort's simulated P&L is <= $0 OR its simulated WR is < 0.24, this candidate goes to the graveyard as 'the ATM tier's floor-clearance advantage does not survive being scoped to only the ticks OTM-2 could never have traded' -- i.e. even isolating the rail's mixed population down to the pure participation-unlock subset does not rescue the idea, and V15_BOLD_CORE_TIERS is retired from ANY future bold rescue proposal, not just this one. That is a real possible outcome, written down before the shadow data exists.
what_would_falsify_the_whole_idea: If rescue_would_clear_floor stays below ~0.35 (i.e. the $2K-$10K ATM band behaves like the OLD $0-2K OTM-3 band's 0.3376 clearance rather than the $0-2K ATM band's 0.9688), the premise that 'ATM-class pricing reliably clears the floor in the afternoon' does not generalize to this equity tier and the whole rescue concept is moot regardless of P&L -- there would be nothing to rescue most of the time.
two_site_invariant_note: backtest/tests/test_bold_tier_revert_2026_08_20.py pins that heartbeat_core.py and setup/scripts/j_intent_executor.py resolve the SAME PRIMARY bold tier symbol (currently V15_BOLD_TIERS at both sites -- verified this session: heartbeat_core.py:2616, j_intent_executor.py:331). This candidate does NOT touch that primary resolution at all -- the rescue is a SECONDARY, additive re-price that only fires AFTER a SKIP_MIN_PREMIUM_FLOOR verdict, so the existing guard's regex-based check keeps passing unchanged. But that guard does NOT (and structurally cannot, as written) detect a NEW divergence this candidate could introduce: rescue logic added to heartbeat_core.py but not to j_intent_executor.py, or vice versa. Per the task's explicit requirement, any implementation must touch BOTH paths or explicitly, deliberately touch NEITHER for the un-rescued path (see candidate_rule.explicitly_out_of_scope above, which chooses 'neither' for j_intent_executor.py with a stated reason) -- and whichever choice is made must ship its own guard test in the same commit, the way test_bold_tier_revert_2026_08_20.py itself does. A silent asymmetry that ships without a test is exactly the L214/L228-class shared-surface drift this project's C34 lesson exists to catch.
